name: Maxim and Array
description: Recently Maxim has found an array of n integers, needed by no one. He immediately come up with idea of changing it: he invented positive integer x and decided to add or subtract it from arbitrary array elements. Formally, by applying single operation Maxim chooses integer i ( 1 ≤ i ≤ n ) and replaces the i -th element of array a i either with a i + x or with a i - x . Please note that the operation may be applied more than once to the same position. Maxim is a curious minimalis, thus he wants to know what is the minimum value that the product of all array elements (i.e. ) can reach, if Maxim would apply no more than k operations to it. Please help him in that.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains three integers n , k and x ( 1 ≤ n , k ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ x ≤ 10 9 ) — the number of elements in the array, the maximum number of operations and the number invented by Maxim, respectively. The second line contains n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n ( ) — the elements of the array found by Maxim.
output_specification: Print n integers b 1 , b 2 , ..., b n in the only line — the array elements after applying no more than k operations to the array. In particular, should stay true for every 1 ≤ i ≤ n , but the product of all array elements should be minimum possible . If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
approach_summary: Maintain prefix sums and dynamic point updates via Fenwick tree using lowbit operations (i & -i) in O(log N) time and O(N) space.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 721D — Maxim and Array [70. BIT / Fenwick Tree]
topic_editorial.summary: Point updates and range prefix queries with Fenwick Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every integer $i$ has a unique binary decomposition. Index $i$ in a Binary Indexed Tree stores the cumulative sum of the interval $(i - \text{lowbit}(i), i]$, allowing logarithmic traversal via $i \mathrel{+}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$ and $i \mathrel{-}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$.
